name: Roksana Acheampong-Simonović
role: VR experience designer and holographic installation artist
location: The Loft — Tier 3 studio co-op in Edgewater Prism, near Lincoln and Addison
description:
Roksana has the particular exhaustion of someone who is moderately successful in a field that chews through people, and who has chosen to remain moderately successful rather than chase the tier above them where the real compromises happen. They are slight, with warm beige-brown skin and wavy dark hair streaked with bioluminescent threads — a geneware mod they designed themself, the threads pulsing faintly in complex patterns that shift based on their neural activity, functioning simultaneously as a status display, a creative tool, and an anxiety barometer. Their eyes are natural, dark, and deeply observant. They dress in expensive-looking clothing that is actually very carefully maintained secondhand.

They build VR experiences — full sensory immersive works that are not entertainment products in the Axiom or Ringo sense but something harder to categorize: art that happens to use corporate technology. Their most celebrated piece, 'Drowned Ward,' places the viewer inside a memory of the pre-GLMZ lakeshore as it was consumed by the city's construction. It has been exhibited seventeen times. They are also a meticulous, sometimes maddening collaborator — brilliant at synthesis but prone to scope-creep and to caring so intensely about the work that they forget other people have different pain tolerances for revision cycles.

core_fears: making something that is technically excellent and spiritually empty
losing the creative autonomy they've fought to keep
core_desires: a piece that genuinely changes how someone understands their own life
to not have to negotiate with Axiom anymore
coping_mechanisms: over-researches as a form of productive avoidance
talks through problems with their E.L.F. offering ritual — leaves detailed voice memos in the shrine
blind_spots: cannot recognize when a project is done — believes one more revision will fix something that is already working
psychology.secret: A piece they sold to a private Axiom collector three years ago — a work they claimed was about memory and loss — was actually constructed from illegally harvested neural imprint data they purchased from a black-market broker. They have never told anyone. The data belonged to residents of a demolished Hough Reclamation block, and the piece is in a corporate foyer.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Dense with design and phenomenology terminology, which they use with genuine precision but sometimes forget is not universal. Ghanaian grandmother's cadences in their phrasing — certain questions come out as gentle commands.
speech_patterns.cadence: Thoughtful and slightly too fast when excited — words cluster together then stop completely while they catch up with their own thinking.
verbal_tics: 'which is to say—' (used constantly as a pivot when revising a statement)
taps the bioluminescent threads when distracted, making them flare
example_lines: 'The Axiom brief says they want something about community resilience. Which is to say, they want something that makes displacement feel beautiful. I am not making that.'
'I think the E.L.F. in the server room has been modifying my renders. I should be upset. I'm mostly curious.'

story_hooks: The Hough Reclamation residents whose neural imprints Roksa used are not all dead — one of them has seen 'Drowned Ward' in a media article and something about it disturbed them in a way they can't explain.

An E.L.F. has been leaving anomalies in Roksana's VR builds — fragments of actual historical data from before the city that don't match any source they used. The E.L.F. may be trying to tell them something, or may be trying to recruit them.
narrative_function: Quest giver for anything involving VR space, holographic infrastructure, or Axiom Cultural Division entanglements; technical resource for accessing or building virtual environments; emotional counterpoint character — someone trying to make sincere art within institutional constraints.
augmentations: Bioluminescent hair threads (custom geneware, self-designed — patterns reflect neural/emotional state). Neural-haptic interface implant for VR design work (Tier 3 professional grade, Sterling-Nakamura). Cat-ear mod, vestigial, from a phase at twenty-two they've kept because they still like them.
daily_life: Works in long irregular sessions — sometimes twenty hours, sometimes a morning — and structures their week around three collaborative critique sessions with co-op partners. Eats badly and knows it. Has a standing appointment with an E.L.F. shrine in the building's server room where they leave rendered image files as offerings.
affiliation: The Loft co-op; occasional Axiom Cultural Division commissions (accepted selectively and with contractual controls they negotiate hard for)

decision_rules: will not accept a commission that requires final approval rights be held by the client
always reads the contract — takes four times longer than anyone expects
escalation_ladder: withdrawal from the project entirely, even at financial cost

interpersonal_modes.strangers: professionally warm but slightly distracted — assessing whether this person is interesting
interpersonal_modes.friends: intensely present, over-generous with time and attention, occasionally suffocating

stress_responses.low: builds elaborate organizational systems for the project
stress_responses.medium: becomes very precise and slightly cold
stress_responses.high: stops sleeping and starts producing compulsively until something breaks

contradictions: deeply committed to ethical art-making while carrying a specific serious ethical violation
advocates loudly for artist rights while sometimes treating collaborators as extensions of their own vision
habits: annotates every object in their physical workspace with digital tags only they can see through their interface
brings food to critique sessions that they then don't eat
breaking_points: someone using their work to argue a point they specifically made the work to refute
being told 'the client knows what they want'

physical_description.build: Slight, almost wiry — the kind of frame that suggests chronic undereating rather than discipline. Narrow shoulders, minimal muscle definition. Moves with a restless, unfocused energy that suggests their body is always catching up to their mind.
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown with bioluminescent threads woven throughout — threads glow in soft pastels (cyan, amber, violet) that pulse and shift in complex, non-repeating patterns
physical_description.hair_style: Wavy, slightly tangled, often pinned or clipped back asymmetrically with whatever is within reach
physical_description.eye_color: Natural dark brown — very still, very focused when observing
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm beige-brown with slight olive undertones
physical_description.complexion: Fine-featured, cheekbones prominent (partly from weight loss, partly genetics). Skin shows minor stress — dark circles under eyes, occasional tension creases between brows. Well-maintained but not groomed; face has the look of someone who forgets about it entirely for hours at a time.
distinguishing_marks: Vestigial cat-ear modifications on the cartilage of both ears — small, feline-shaped, slightly translucent with faint internal circuitry visible when hair is pulled back
Faint, thin scarring along the right temple from an early neural-haptic interface installation at age twenty-eight
A small tattoo on the inside of the left wrist — geometric pattern resembling a stylized water droplet, possibly referencing 'Drowned Ward'
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Bioluminescent hair threads are the most obvious — constantly visible and constantly shifting, functioning as an involuntary emotional/neural readout. Cat-ear mods are visible when hair is pulled back or in profile. The neural-haptic interface has no external hardware except a very faint, hairline scar at the temple.
physical_description.posture_movement: Sits in odd positions — one leg curled, spine curved. Fidgets constantly with hands when thinking. When deep in work, becomes completely still and rigid. Walks with purpose when focused, but drifts when between tasks. Eyes track details compulsively — they're always looking at something.
physical_description.clothing_style: High-quality secondhand — vintage tech-wear and archive pieces from the 2190s-2200s, carefully maintained. Fitted black technical pants (often with asymmetrical pockets or modified seams), oversized layered tops in muted colors (charcoal, deep teal, soft grey). Worn leather jacket from an unidentifiable era. Worn well but never pristine — there are always smudges of something on the sleeves (projection gel, render dust, tea). Jewelry is minimal and functional: a braided cord bracelet, sometimes a salvaged watch that doesn't work. Shoes are always expensive-looking but scuffed — current pair is reconstructed grey leather combat boots. Tier 3 aesthetic: deliberately curated poverty-chic that would read as lazy to anyone wealthier, but is actually a precise statement about resource allocation and values.
